compounds.name: Semaglutide
compounds.summary: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist with ~7-day half-life; weekly SC injection is the common prescribed cadence.
compounds.whatItIs: Semaglutide is a modified GLP-1 analog approved for type 2 diabetes and chronic weight management in several regions. Structurally it resembles native GLP-1 with alterations that slow clearance and allow less frequent dosing than first-generation daily agents.
compounds.mechanism: Activates the GLP-1 receptor, which influences insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner, slows gastric emptying, and reduces appetite signaling. It is not insulin and does not replace medical supervision.
highlights: Once-weekly SC dosing is standard in approved labeling
Titration schedules start low and increase over weeks
Steady state often discussed after ~4–5 weeks of weekly use
Often logged with injection site and weekly weigh-in notes

reportedPatterns.amountDescription: 0.25 mg → 0.5 mg → 1 mg → up to 2 mg weekly
reportedPatterns.notes: Label describes stepwise titration over 4+ weeks at each step; individual plans vary.
Separate oral formulation (Rybelsus); absorption differs from injectable.

loggingTips: Log day/time of injection and any site rotation
Note titration step when your prescriber changes strength
Track appetite, nausea, or other observations neutrally

sources.title: Clinical Pharmacokinetics of Semaglutide — systematic review

compounds.caution: Prescribing information is for licensed medical use only. This app records what you enter and does not suggest doses or treatment plans.

compounds.name: Tirzepatide
compounds.summary: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist with ~5-day half-life; weekly SC injection with label-defined titration.
compounds.whatItIs: Tirzepatide is a once-weekly injectable that activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. It is approved for type 2 diabetes and, in some regions, chronic weight management under separate brand names.
compounds.mechanism: Combines incretin pathway activation (GLP-1) with GIP receptor activity. Effects on glucose and appetite are studied in large trials; individual response varies widely.
compounds.tmax: Varies by dose; peak exposure within first day after injection
highlights: Weekly SC administration in approved labeling
Titration from 2.5 mg upward in 2.5 mg steps
Missed-dose windows described in product labeling
Often paired with blood glucose or weight logs

reportedPatterns.amountDescription: 2.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 5 mg weekly
reportedPatterns.notes: Initial 2.5 mg phase is for tolerability, not glycemic effect per label.

reportedPatterns.amountDescription: 5 mg → 7.5 mg → 10 mg → 12.5 mg → 15 mg weekly
reportedPatterns.notes: Increases of 2.5 mg after ≥4 weeks on current dose when additional effect is needed.

loggingTips: Record injection day to keep a consistent weekly rhythm
Note GI side effects during titration weeks
Log concurrent medications only as personal reference
compounds.caution: Not studied for type 1 diabetes in labeling. This tracker does not provide medical advice or dosing guidance.

compounds.name: Liraglutide
compounds.summary: Daily GLP-1 agonist with ~13-hour half-life; shorter acting than weekly semaglutide or tirzepatide.
compounds.whatItIs: Liraglutide is an acylated GLP-1 analog approved for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Its shorter half-life requires daily subcutaneous injection compared with weekly GLP-1 agents.
compounds.mechanism: GLP-1 receptor activation with albumin binding that extends action to roughly half a day. Appetite and gastric emptying effects are similar in class to other GLP-1 RAs but with a different PK profile.
highlights: Daily dosing cadence (unlike weekly semaglutide/tirzepatide)
Label includes titration from low starting dose
Useful comparison reference when switching GLP-1 agents
Log time-of-day for consistency

reportedPatterns.notes: Start 0.6 mg for 1 week minimum before increasing per label.
Multi-week titration schedule in label; discontinue if 3 mg not tolerated.

loggingTips: Same time each day helps compare appetite notes
Track pen strength when titrating
Note injection site if rotating

sources.title: GLP-1 agonists review — Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism 2024

compounds.caution: Daily GLP-1 agents differ from weekly ones in timing and side-effect profile. Consult your prescriber for any switch.

compounds.name: BPC-157
compounds.summary: 15-amino-acid gastric peptide fragment studied mainly in preclinical models; widely discussed for local repair logging.
compounds.whatItIs: BPC-157 is a synthetic peptide derived from a protective protein found in gastric juice. Most published work is preclinical (rodent models). Human clinical trials for musculoskeletal use are limited; it is not FDA-approved as a drug.
compounds.mechanism: Preclinical studies describe effects on angiogenesis, nitric oxide pathways, and tendon/ligament healing models. Human mechanism data at therapeutic doses is sparse.
highlights: Microgram (mcg) amounts dominate community literature
Often paired with TB-500 in 'Wolverine' stacks
Preclinical-heavy evidence base
Log injury site and subjective recovery notes neutrally

reportedPatterns.notes: Often injected SC near the area of interest; some split into morning/evening.
Cycle length varies; breaks between cycles commonly discussed.
Systemic repair discussions usually emphasize injectable routes.

loggingTips: Use mcg units consistently in your log
Note injection site and which side/limb
Track cycle start/end dates for your own records

sources.title: BPC-157 preclinical literature — Sikiric group reviews
Community protocol surveys — r/Peptides / practitioner summaries

compounds.caution: Research chemical; purity and legality vary by region. No approved human dose exists. Not medical advice.

compounds.name: TB-500
compounds.summary: Actin-binding peptide fragment discussed for systemic repair; milligram (mg) weekly amounts in community literature.
compounds.whatItIs: TB-500 typically refers to a synthetic fragment (often amino acids 17–23) related to thymosin beta-4. It is studied in animal models for wound healing and actin regulation. Not an FDA-approved therapeutic.
compounds.mechanism: Binds actin and is proposed to support cell migration and angiogenesis in preclinical models. Systemic distribution is a reason it is often paired with locally acting BPC-157 in community protocols.
highlights: Dosed in milligrams, not micrograms (unlike BPC-157)
Loading + maintenance phases appear in community write-ups
WADA-prohibited for tested athletes
Log weekly totals to avoid double-counting

reportedPatterns.notes: Often Mon/Thu split; loading duration 2–4 weeks in write-ups.
Reduced after loading in many described cycles.
No randomized trial of the combination in humans.

loggingTips: Record mg amount and injection day clearly
Mark loading vs maintenance phase in notes
Track total weekly mg for your own adherence view
compounds.caution: Research use only in most jurisdictions. Angiogenesis-related theoretical concerns are discussed in literature — not evaluated by this app.

compounds.name: GHK-Cu
compounds.summary: Endogenous copper-binding tripeptide; topical use is well discussed, injectable human data is limited.
compounds.whatItIs: GHK-Cu (gly-his-lys + copper) is a naturally occurring peptide involved in wound healing and collagen signaling in vitro. Cosmetic topicals are common; systemic injectable use is mostly extrapolated from animal work.
compounds.mechanism: Modulates gene expression related to extracellular matrix, inflammation, and tissue remodeling in cell and animal models. Copper moiety participates in redox and enzymatic chemistry.
highlights: Strong topical evidence vs sparse injectable human PK
Rapid peptide clearance → multiple daily doses in some SC discussions
Often logged for skin or joint-adjacent protocols
Distinguish topical from injectable in your records

reportedPatterns.notes: Facial skin trials used twice-daily application for 12 weeks.
Extrapolated from rodent mg/kg; not validated in controlled human studies.

loggingTips: Tag route (topical vs injectable) in notes
For SC logs, record mg and time of day
Cycle length (4–8 weeks) often noted in community write-ups

sources.title: Topical facial skin trials — Leyden et al.

compounds.caution: Injectable human dosing is not established in published trials. Copper balance matters — this app does not assess safety.

compounds.name: Sermorelin
compounds.summary: Short-acting GHRH analog; ~10–20 min half-life; pulsatile GH stimulation.
compounds.whatItIs: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone. It was FDA-approved (Geref) for pediatric GH deficiency testing/therapy but was discontinued commercially in the US. Compounded forms appear in longevity clinics.
compounds.mechanism: Binds GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotrophs to stimulate endogenous GH release in a pulse. Does not contain exogenous GH.
highlights: Very short half-life → multiple daily or nightly doses in practice
Often combined with a GHRP (e.g. ipamorelin) in write-ups
Historical FDA product vs modern compounded supply
Log timing relative to sleep or fasted state if you track that

reportedPatterns.notes: Night dosing aligns with natural nocturnal GH pulse in some protocols.
Synergy is theoretical; monitor for flushing or water retention.

loggingTips: Record mcg and time; short half-life makes timing meaningful
Note sleep quality or fasting state neutrally
Track 'on/off' cycle weeks if you use them
compounds.caution: GH axis modulation has endocrine implications. Not for unsupervised use. Tracker only.

compounds.name: CJC-1295 (no DAC)
compounds.summary: Modified GHRH analog without albumin binding; ~30 min half-life; common stack partner for ipamorelin.
compounds.whatItIs: CJC-1295 without the Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) is a shortened, modified GHRH analog designed for a brief GH-releasing pulse. It is sold as a research peptide and is not FDA-approved for general use.
compounds.mechanism: GHRH receptor agonism with four amino-acid substitutions vs native GHRH(1-29), extending action slightly vs sermorelin while staying pulsatile.
highlights: Preferred over DAC version when pulsatility is desired
Typical stack: equal mcg with ipamorelin
2–3× daily timing in community protocols
Do not confuse mcg (GHRH) with mg (TB-500) units

reportedPatterns.notes: Often morning + pre-bed; fasted state discussed.
Most common ratio in written protocols; individual variation is wide.

loggingTips: Log each injection time separately for short half-life agents
Note if taken with ipamorelin in same entry
Track cycle breaks (e.g. 5 on / 2 off) in notes
compounds.caution: Research peptide. GH/IGF-1 effects vary. Not a dose recommendation from this app.

compounds.name: CJC-1295 (with DAC)
compounds.summary: Albumin-binding GHRH analog with multi-day half-life; sustained GH elevation vs pulsatile protocols.
compounds.whatItIs: The DAC (Drug Affinity Complex) variant binds serum albumin, extending circulation time to roughly a week. This produces sustained GH/IGF-1 exposure rather than discrete pulses — a different pharmacologic profile from Mod GRF 1-29.
compounds.mechanism: Same GHRH receptor target as other analogs, but prolonged exposure from albumin binding alters the pulsatility pattern that pituitary physiology normally uses.
highlights: Weekly or twice-weekly injection schedules in write-ups
Different profile from no-DAC + ipamorelin stacks
Long washout if side effects occur
Log injection day and any water retention notes

reportedPatterns.notes: Less common than no-DAC in modern stack discussions.
Rodent/human PK papers describe prolonged IGF-1 elevation.

loggingTips: Weekly cadence — set a recurring reminder day
Note any prolonged side effects given long half-life
Separate log entry from daily GHRP stacks

sources.title: CJC-1295 DAC PK — Teichman et al.

compounds.caution: Sustained GH elevation differs from pulsatile protocols. Medical supervision is essential if used clinically.

compounds.name: Ipamorelin
compounds.summary: Selective ghrelin/GHS-R agonist; ~2 h half-life; often stacked with Mod GRF 1-29.
compounds.whatItIs: Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide growth hormone secretagogue described as more selective than older GHRPs (less cortisol/prolactin release in animal models). Sold as research material; not FDA-approved for OTC use.
compounds.mechanism: Activates GHS-R1a (ghrelin receptor) on pituitary to trigger a GH pulse. Works synergistically with GHRH-class peptides in combined protocols.
highlights: mcg dosing; often 100–300 mcg per injection
Pairs with CJC-1295 no DAC or sermorelin
2–3× daily timing common in literature
Log hunger or flushing neutrally post-injection

reportedPatterns.notes: Pre-bed dose aligns with nocturnal GH discussions.
Same syringe administration often described.

loggingTips: Use mcg in amount field consistently
Note stacked peptides in the same log entry
Track cycle breaks to mirror your own schedule
compounds.caution: GH axis effects are individual. Research peptide purity varies. Not medical guidance.

compounds.name: Tesamorelin
compounds.summary: FDA-approved GHRH analog (1-44) for HIV-associated lipodystrophy; daily SC dosing in labeling.
compounds.whatItIs: Tesamorelin is a stabilized GHRH(1-44) analog with an N-terminal modification that reduces enzymatic degradation. Unlike research CJC variants, it has an approved indication with defined labeling.
compounds.mechanism: GHRH receptor activation with longer exposure than native GHRH fragments. Approved use is specific to visceral adipose reduction in HIV lipodystrophy — not a general wellness indication.
highlights: Rare example of FDA-approved injectable GHRH analog
Daily dosing in approved labeling
Distinct indication vs cosmetic GH use
Log as daily mcg/mg per your prescription label

reportedPatterns.notes: Indication-specific; not generalized to other populations in labeling.

loggingTips: Record daily injection time
Note indication context in private notes if helpful
Track abdominal measurements only as personal data
compounds.caution: Approved only for specific HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Off-label context is not endorsed by this app.

compounds.name: AOD-9604
compounds.summary: GH fragment peptide studied for lipolysis in models; microgram daily amounts in community literature.
compounds.whatItIs: AOD-9604 is a modified fragment of human growth hormone (amino acids 176–191) marketed in research channels for metabolic effects. It does not raise IGF-1 like full GH secretagogues in some preclinical descriptions.
compounds.mechanism: Proposed to stimulate lipolysis without full GH axis activation in animal models. Human efficacy data is limited and inconsistent.
highlights: mcg-range dosing in community write-ups
Often morning fasted injection timing discussed
Distinct from GH secretagogue stacks
Log separately from GHRH/GHRP protocols

reportedPatterns.notes: Fasted state often mentioned; evidence base is weak.
Break periods between cycles commonly described.

loggingTips: Use mcg units
Note fasting state if you track it
Keep separate from GH stack logs for clarity
compounds.caution: Not FDA-approved. Weight-related claims in marketing exceed published human evidence.

compounds.name: MOTS-c
compounds.summary: Mitochondrial-derived peptide discussed for metabolic exercise mimetic effects; emerging human data.
compounds.whatItIs: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA. Research explores roles in glucose metabolism, exercise response, and aging models. Injectable use in humans is mostly early-stage.
compounds.mechanism: Activates AMPK-related pathways in cell and animal models, influencing glucose uptake and fatty acid oxidation. Mechanism in humans at injectable doses is still being studied.
highlights: mg-range weekly or biweekly patterns in early discussions
Metabolic logging pairs well with exercise notes
Distinct from GLP-1 class agents
Evidence still evolving — attribute carefully

reportedPatterns.notes: Wide variance; some protocols use short 2–4 week courses.
Often combined with training logs rather than daily dosing.

loggingTips: Log mg amount and weekly injection day
Note training sessions on the same day if relevant
Track energy or glucose readings only as personal notes
